title: A Cipher for the Parish
premise: When insurance investigator Mirabel Dunmore is called to the fog-bound parish of St. Aldhelm's to assess a claim on missing schoolteacher Edith Vane, she discovers Edith's diary in the church vestry — and its entries continue three weeks past the date of her disappearance, written in a hand that isn't quite Edith's. As Mirabel's photographic memory unlocks the diary's cipher of hymn numbers and grave plots, she realizes the killer is someone inside the investigation itself, feeding on her every move. The trail leads to the parish's charitable trust, where Edith had uncovered decades of embezzlement tied to an old drowning the village never questioned. In the climax at the flooded crypt beneath the church, Mirabel turns her own case file into bait, forcing the killer — the coroner who certified all those 'accidents' — to confess before witnesses; the truth costs her nearly her life but restores Edith's name and breaks the trust's grip on the parish.
about_author: Ivo Sandoval is the pen name of a former rural claims adjuster who spent fifteen years reading other people's disasters in small-town England. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet villages, and the arithmetic of guilt.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Mirabel arrives in St. Aldhelm's to process the life-insurance claim on missing teacher Edith Vane, whose body was never found. POV: Mirabel. She notices the vicar flinches at Edith's name. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack into curiosity.

chapters.title: Hymn Numbers
chapters.summary: In the vestry, Mirabel finds Edith's diary hidden behind a hymnal, its final entries written after her disappearance in subtly altered handwriting. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession as memory and evidence refuse to align.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Verdicts
chapters.summary: Mirabel pulls records of three past 'accidental' deaths in the parish and spots identical procedural shortcuts signed by coroner Dr. Ambrose Pell. POV: Mirabel with flashbacks of prior cases. Emotional beat: cold recognition that this village has practice at burying things.

chapters.title: Grave Plots and Grace Notes
chapters.summary: Decoding the diary's cipher of hymn numbers mapped onto gravestones, Mirabel finds Edith photographed the trust's ledgers. POV: alternating Mirabel and reconstructed Edith diary voice. Emotional beat: growing intimacy with a woman she'll never meet.

chapters.title: The Trustee's Welcome
chapters.summary: Charitable trust chairman Harold Fenwick charms Mirabel over sherry while warning her off 'conspiracy talk.' POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the first taste of how power smiles while it closes doors.

chapters.title: What the Constable Knew
chapters.summary: Retired constable Bill Trewin admits he was ordered to close Edith's case in forty-eight hours — by Pell. POV: Trewin then Mirabel. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling; an old man's shame becomes her first ally.

chapters.title: The Drowning Nobody Questioned
chapters.summary: Edith's research points to a 1987 drowning in the mill race — the trust's founding scandal. POV: Mirabel interviewing the drowned man's sister. Emotional beat: grief across decades, and the realization inheritance here means silence.

chapters.title: A Page Torn Out
chapters.summary: The diary's binding shows a removed page; someone has been inside Mirabel's room. POV: Mirabel, paranoid second-person interludes. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also hunted.

chapters.title: Sergeant Quill
chapters.summary: Young police sergeant Dana Quill, assigned to 'assist,' mirrors Mirabel's questions back at her too precisely. POV: Quill. Emotional beat: ambiguity — eager ally or the killer's eyes?

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Following the cipher underground, Mirabel finds a bricked alcove behind the crypt wall and fresh mortar. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: dread made physical; the parish literally built on its secrets.

chapters.title: Fenwick Falls
chapters.summary: Harold Fenwick is found dead at the foot of the tower stairs — ruled a fall. POV: Mirabel arriving too late. Emotional beat: fury and fear; the killer is erasing the list faster than she can read it.

chapters.title: Quill's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered, Quill admits Pell recruited her to monitor investigators, insisting she never knew it would turn lethal. POV: Quill. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth embodied; betrayal offered as penance.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Graphological analysis confirms the post-disappearance diary entries were forged by someone practicing Edith's hand for years — Pell kept samples from death certificates. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: horror at patience like this.

chapters.title: What Edith Found
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the torn page from Mirabel's memory of a photograph edge, she recovers Edith's full ledger evidence and a meeting appointment dated the night she vanished. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by grief — Edith died holding proof.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Baited
chapters.summary: Mirabel leaks a fabricated case file naming a false witness, knowing the killer will move against it. POV: Mirabel planning, Quill doubting. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into ruthlessness.

chapters.title: Night at the Mill
chapters.summary: The false witness is attacked at the derelict mill; Mirabel intervenes and glimpses Pell fleeing, confirming him. POV: Mirabel, near-fatal chase. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into certainty.

chapters.title: Pell's Sermon
chapters.summary: Confronted quietly, Pell argues he protected the parish from ruin, casting himself as shepherd. POV: Pell. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of corruption; Mirabel almost understands him.

chapters.title: The Flooded Crypt
chapters.summary: Lured by a forged diary entry in her own hand, Mirabel is trapped in the rising undercroft — Pell intends a fourth accident. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: drowning in the archive of the parish's sins.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Quill and Trewin arrive; Pell, cornered above the floodwater, confesses to four deaths to save himself from the water he chose for others. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: truth extracted at knifepoint, witnessed and undeniable.

chapters.title: Edith's Resting Place
chapters.summary: Behind the fresh mortar they find Edith's remains and her final ledger page clutched in a waterproof sleeve. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: mourning finally given a body and a name.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: The trust collapses; the claim is paid to Edith's estranged sister along with the truth. POV: Mirabel closing the file. Emotional beat: justice as paperwork — unglamorous, complete.

chapters.title: A Clean Page
chapters.summary: Leaving St. Aldhelm's, Mirabel mails her own coded account of the case to a journalist, choosing truth over the comfortable silence she was offered. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined; the investigator becomes witness.
